deep.reconstruction: This page has no mathematics. It is a fragment of a letter draft on a torn, L-shaped piece of paper. The whole text, in German Kurrent script, is a salutation centred near the top, 'Hochgeehrtester Herr Professor!' ('Most highly esteemed Professor!'), and one opening line lower down: 'Ihr gütiges Anerbieten, meinen Aufsatz über die Theorie ...' ('Your kind offer [to ...] my essay on the theory ...'). The sentence stops after 'Theorie'. The rest of the sheet is blank, and the missing lower-right part may never have been written on. Riemann apparently began a reply to a professor who had offered to do something with an essay of his, probably publish, forward or review it, and then abandoned the draft. The sheet was later reused, or bundled, with mathematical notes. The previous page has a quadruple integral of the form ∫dx dy dx' dy'/(uu+vv+u'u'+v'v') with Jacobian-type 2×2 minors. The next page derives the components of the curl of (X,Y,Z) from circulation around a small rectangle, in an electrical context. Neither derivation continues onto this page. Which essay is meant is not determinable from the page. One guess consistent with an essay on a physical 'Theorie' and with the electrical material nearby is Riemann's 'Zur Theorie der Nobili'schen Farbenringe' (Poggendorffs Annalen, 1855); the addressee could then be Poggendorff or W. Weber. This identification is mine and speculative; the text does not support it beyond the word 'Theorie'. There is nothing to reconstruct mathematically.
